observations: Seed goal is (churn neil liz) but the fragment binds ?him=NEIL ?her=LIZ, argument order of churn matches (churn ?him ?her).

do-divorce prints as (DO-DIVORCE TONY LIZ): ?him in the fragment's (do-divorce ?him ?her) appears to be bound to the husband here, not to NEIL. Either the trace shows a different subgoal form than Fig. 2 or DIVORCE re-orders arguments. UNRESOLVED (Q-PF-2).
The disjunction (or (churn ...) (together ...)) is resolved to the together branch, which fails with 'no acceptable plans'. Why churn was not chosen is not explained. UNRESOLVED (Q-PL-3).

The paper states each subgoal had exactly one usable fragment in the library at the time (L85-TR p. 8), although several are listed as candidates, candidates are listed before constraint filtering, or the others failed constraints. UNRESOLVED (Q-PL-4).
